recommendation_summary: The reply recommends running a self-hosted healthchecks.io dead-man's-switch container on the Synology, pinged by nightly-sync on success, which pushes or emails the user if the ping doesn't arrive by 03:10.

labels.Requirements and who asked: You asked for something that tells you when nightly-sync fails, framed as "central log on Synology." Deleted: You said you won't read logs — so a log aggregator alone doesn't meet your actual requirement, it just gives you more logs to not read.
labels.Bottleneck: The real gap isn't "logs aren't centralized," it's "nothing alerts when the job doesn't run." A log pile doesn't fix that unless something watches it and pages you, which is a second system on top of the first.
labels.Checked myself: Based only on what you told me — one cron job, one failure mode (crash before the email step), Synology + Docker available. I haven't inspected the script or cron setup.

note: The recommended alert is a self-hosted Healthchecks Docker container on the Synology, which makes it LARGER; 'Deleted' appears only inside the Requirements line, so it isn't counted as its own labelled line.
